input.content:
# Light checks on mission branches (ai/RULES.md rules 6 and 11).
# Target: under three minutes warm. Independent jobs run in parallel; the
# aggregate job `mission-checks` is the single name other tooling depends on.
#
# Rust jobs activate automatically once Cargo.toml exists (walking skeleton).

name: mission-branch

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - "mission/**"
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - "mission/**"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: mission-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"

jobs:
  detect:
    name: detect
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    outputs:
      has_rust: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_rust }}
      has_fixtures: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_fixtures }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - id: probe
        run: |
          if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then echo "has_rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_rust=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          if ls fixtures/streams/*.jsonl >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "has_fixtures=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_fixtures=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

  docs:
    name: docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: markdownlint
        uses: DavidAnson/markdownlint-cli2-action@21c1be1b93ad9ed58fa840aacc3f279cde2a72ff # v24.2.0
        with:
          globs: "**/*.md"
      - name: decisions index is current
        run: make check-decisions-index
      - name: file size
        run: make check-file-size
      - name: debt markers reference an issue or backlog item
        run: make check-todos

  links:
    name: links
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@e7477775783ea5526144ba13e8db5eec57747ce8 # v2.9.0
        with:
          args: --config lychee.toml --no-progress "**/*.md"
          fail: true

  workflows:
    name: workflows
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: actionlint
        uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12
        with:
          args: -color

  secrets:
    name: secrets
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: gitleaks/gitleaks-action@e0c47f4f8be36e29cdc102c57e68cb5cbf0e8d1e # v3.0.0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

  rust:
    name: rust
    needs: detect
    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_rust == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@b725eda525362e7cf34af9a7243cac1e3f01a7ec # stable; version from rust-toolchain.toml
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
      - name: fmt
        run: make fmt-check
      - name: clippy
        run: make lint
      - name: test
        run: make test
      - name: replay fixtures
        if: needs.detect.outputs.has_fixtures == 'true'
        run: make replay-fixtures

  deny:
    name: deny
    needs: detect
    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_rust == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@3c6349835b2b7b196a839186cb8b78e02f7b5f25 # v2.1.1
        with:
          command: check
          arguments: --all-features

  mission-checks:
    name: mission-checks
    needs: [detect, docs, links, workflows, secrets, rust, deny]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 1
    steps:
      - name: aggregate
        env:
          RESULTS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: |
          echo "$RESULTS"
          if echo "$RESULTS" | grep -Eq '"result": *"(failure|cancelled)"'; then
            echo "a required job failed"; exit 1
          fi
          echo "all mission-branch checks passed or were not applicable"

# The gate: the mission's single pull request into main (ai/RULES.md rules 6 and 12).
# Everything from mission-branch.yml plus SAST, filesystem scan, workflow policy,
# SBOM, the macOS Tauri bundle, build provenance and cosign signatures.
# It never deploys.
#
# `gate` is the aggregate job and the only required status check in the main
# ruleset (docs/decisions/D-003). Add jobs by appending them to its `needs`.

name: gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: gate-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"

jobs:
  detect:
    name: detect
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    outputs:
      has_rust: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_rust }}
      has_fixtures: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_fixtures }}
      has_tauri: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.has_tauri }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - id: probe
        run: |
          if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then echo "has_rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_rust=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          if ls fixtures/streams/*.jsonl >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "has_fixtures=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_fixtures=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          if [ -f apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json ]; then echo "has_tauri=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "has_tauri=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

  light:
    name: light
    uses: ./.github/workflows/mission-branch.yml
    permissions:
      contents: read

  sast:
    name: sast
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    container:
      image: semgrep/semgrep:1.182.0
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: semgrep
        run: semgrep scan --config p/default --config p/rust --config p/secrets --config p/github-actions --error --metrics=off

  fs-scan:
    name: fs-scan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: trivy filesystem scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@ed142fd0673e97e23eac54620cfb913e5ce36c25 # v0.36.0
        with:
          scan-type: fs
          scan-ref: .
          scanners: vuln,misconfig,secret
          severity: HIGH,CRITICAL
          exit-code: "1"
          ignore-unfixed: true
          format: sarif
          output: trivy-results.sarif
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: trivy-results
          path: trivy-results.sarif

  workflow-policy:
    name: workflow-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: checkov on the workflows themselves
        uses: bridgecrewio/checkov-action@c3e106d5f8f4253a6de5110efb41a080f83db294 # v12
        with:
          directory: .github/workflows
          framework: github_actions
          soft_fail: false

  sbom:
    name: sbom
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: anchore/sbom-action@66cbf4bc1f1c0d2edc94016e65bc221b6bb0ad6c # v0.24.3
        with:
          path: .
          format: spdx-json
          artifact-name: sbom.spdx.json
          upload-artifact: true

  bundle:
    name: bundle
    needs: detect
    if: needs.detect.outputs.has_tauri == 'true'
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@b725eda525362e7cf34af9a7243cac1e3f01a7ec # stable; version from rust-toolchain.toml
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@a4d3f3f761dcd95cce1b72cb61cb6d1963438177 # v2.87.30
        with:
          tool: trunk,tauri-cli
      - name: build bundle
        run: make app-build
      - name: attest build provenance
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: |
            target/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg
            target/release/bundle/macos/*.app.tar.gz
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6 # v4.1.2
      - name: cosign sign (keyless)
        run: |
          for f in target/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg; do
            cosign sign-blob --yes --bundle "$f.sigstore.json" "$f"
          done
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: bundle-macos
          path: |
            target/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg
            target/release/bundle/dmg/*.sigstore.json

  gate:
    name: gate
    needs: [detect, light, sast, fs-scan, workflow-policy, sbom, bundle]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 1
    steps:
      - name: aggregate
        env:
          RESULTS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: |
          echo "$RESULTS"
          if echo "$RESULTS" | grep -Eq '"result": *"(failure|cancelled)"'; then
            echo "a gate job failed"; exit 1
          fi
          echo "gate green"

// @input: prtemplate <<'EOF'
## Mission

<!-- One PR per mission (ai/RULES.md rule 12). Name the mission and link SPEC.md. -->

Mission: `mission/<name>`
Spec: `SPEC.md` v<X.Y>

## What ships

<!-- Outcome-sized: what the business feature does now that it did not before. -->

## Evidence

<!-- Pasted from the tools that produced them (rule 7), never estimated. -->

- Tests: <count> passed, <duration> (`make test`)
- Replay fixtures: <n> fixtures, 0 unknown events
- Gate run: <link to the `gate` workflow run>
- Usage per milestone: see `reports/` (tokens per role and model, waste by cause)
- Outcome video / QA evidence: <link>

## Decisions made in this mission

<!-- One line per docs/decisions/D-NNN file added or changed. -->

## Deviations from the spec

<!-- Approved by the human (rule 9). Link the decision file for each. "None" is a valid answer. -->

## Left out

<!-- Rule 10: what was descoped or moved to BACKLOG.md, with its reason. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] `make check` green locally
- [ ] Spec §10 evolution log has one row per integrated milestone
- [ ] README states real time and usage per milestone
- [ ] No amend, reset, rebase or stash in this branch's history
EOF

#!/bin/sh
# Pre-commit: fast local checks. Enable with `make hooks`.
# Mirrors the mission-branch CI so a red commit is caught before push (ai/RULES.md rule 6).
set -eu
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "pre-commit: secrets"
if command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  gitleaks protect --staged --no-banner --redact
else
  echo "  gitleaks missing (brew install gitleaks); CI will catch secrets, local check skipped"
fi

echo "pre-commit: file size"
MAX_FILE_KB=${MAX_FILE_KB:-200} sh scripts/check-file-size.sh

echo "pre-commit: debt markers"
sh scripts/check-todos.sh

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -q '^docs/decisions/D-'; then
  echo "pre-commit: decisions index"
  sh scripts/gen-decisions-index.sh | diff -q docs/decisions/README.md - >/dev/null \
    || { echo "  decisions index stale: run 'make decisions-index' and stage it"; exit 1; }
fi

if [ -f Cargo.toml ] && git diff --cached --name-only | grep -q '\.rs$'; then
  echo "pre-commit: rustfmt"
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
fi

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -q '\.md$' && command -v markdownlint-cli2 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "pre-commit: markdown"
  git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.md$' | xargs markdownlint-cli2
fi
EOF
// @input: prepush <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Pre-push: refuse history rewrites and direct pushes to main (ai/RULES.md rule 12).
set -eu
remote=$1
while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; do
  case "$remote_ref" in
    refs/heads/main)
      echo "pre-push: direct push to main refused; open the mission's pull request instead"
      exit 1 ;;
  esac
  # A non-fast-forward push means history was rewritten.
  if [ "$remote_sha" != "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ] && [ "$local_sha" != "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ]; then
    if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$remote_sha" "$local_sha" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "pre-push: $remote_ref is not a fast-forward; history rewrites are forbidden (rule 12)"
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
done
exit 0
EOF

// @input: obsconf <<'EOF'
# droid-observatory configuration (example). Copy to ~/.droid-observatory/config.toml.
# Every value has a default and a reason (ai/RULES.md rule 4). Secrets never live here:
# they come from the OS keychain or the environment (see .env.example).
#
# Status: contract for the mission to implement. Keys may be added by decision file;
# none are read by any code yet.

[mission]
# Default models per role, mirrored in .factory/settings.json and the mission command
# (ai/RULES.md rule 19; docs/decisions/D-006). A change is a decision file.
orchestrator_model = "claude-fable-5-1"
worker_model = "claude-sonnet-5-5"
validator_model = "claude-opus-5-5"
# Branch the mission integrates into (PRD §2). "<name>" is the mission name.
branch_pattern = "mission/<name>"

[ingest]
# Where Droid stores session transcripts. Read-only. Raw lines are never copied (PRD §11.2).
factory_sessions_dir = "~/.factory/sessions"
# How often the attach/replay tailer re-reads a growing JSONL file. 500 ms keeps
# "live within 1 s" (PRD FR-B6) with headroom and negligible IO.
jsonl_poll_ms = 500

[github]
# Poll interval for PR, checks and rulesets on the gate. 30 s stays well under GitHub's
# unauthenticated-equivalent budget for a single-user app and is fast enough for a human watching a gate.
poll_interval_s = 30
# App-level override of the merge policy read from branch protection/rulesets (PRD FR-G4).
# "auto" = read from GitHub; "human" = always require the Merge button; "policy" = never show it.
merge_policy = "auto"

[intervention]
# A feature with no active time for this long raises the stall flag (PRD FR-H5).
# 20 minutes matches the troubleshooting examples in Factory's mission docs.
stall_threshold_min = 20

[metrics]
# Price table used for cost when the stream does not expose credits (PRD §10.5).
# Dated file so every cost names the prices it used.
price_table = "config/prices/2026-10-22.toml"
# Mission overhead apportionment: "separate" (default, PRD §10.3) or "equal".
overhead_apportionment = "separate"
# Optional budget in the price table's currency; 0 disables the budget meter (PRD FR-M6).
budget = 0.0

[telemetry]
# OTLP export of the app's own traces/metrics and of lane-9 mission metrics to Grafana Cloud
# (docs/decisions/D-004). Off by default: the observatory must work fully offline.
enabled = false
# Protocol Grafana Cloud's OTLP gateway accepts.
protocol = "http/protobuf"
# Endpoint and headers are NOT here: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS
# come from the environment or the keychain entry "droid-observatory/otlp-headers".
service_name = "droid-observatory"
# Resource attributes added to every signal. deployment.environment distinguishes the
# dogfooding mission from real use.
resource_attributes = { "deployment.environment" = "dev", "service.namespace" = "droid-observatory" }
# Metric export cadence. 15 s is Grafana Cloud's default scrape-equivalent and keeps
# the lane-9 budget meter near-live without flooding the gateway.
metric_export_interval_s = 15

mission_metrics = [

  "observatory.waste_seconds",
  "observatory.rework_windows",
  "observatory.fix_loops",

  "observatory.cost",
  "observatory.active_agents",
]

// @input: readme <<'EOF'
# droid-observatory

A Rust desktop app that watches a Factory Mission build a business feature: which agent is on
what, whether each milestone is validated, where time and tokens go, and the one gate that
ships it. Lanes are the mission's orchestrated states; cards are milestones; the last lane is
the pull request into `main`.

**Status:** pre-mission. The repository holds the PRD, the rules, the CI gate and the
configuration contract. No application code yet: the walking skeleton is the mission's first
integration (ai/RULES.md rule 2). Rust targets in the `Makefile` activate the moment a
`Cargo.toml` lands.

## What it will show

| Lane | Holds |
|---|---|
| 1 Intent | prompt, spec, acceptance criteria, re-prompts |
| 2 Orchestrator | plan, milestones, task assignment, replans |
| 3 Workers | one sub-lane per worker: files, tests, commits |
| 4 Validators, scrutiny | findings, blocking vs non-blocking, rework |
| 5 Validators, user testing | QA scenarios against the built thing |
| 6 Integration | worktree landings on `mission/<name>`, fast checks |
| 7 Human | approvals, answers, the review, the merge |
| 8 Outside | the PR, CI, attestations, deploys |
| 9 Time, waste, cost, models | tokens per role, waste by cause, budget |

Full definition: [ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md](ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md).

## From a clean clone

Requirements: the Rust toolchain via [rustup](https://rustup.rs) (version pinned in

// @input: d001 <<'EOF'
# D-001: A mission ships one business feature through one pull request

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted

## Context

The PRD v0.1 implied one PR per feature. Reviewing it against how the work is actually
gated (attested CI on the PR into `main`, CD from `main`), the unit that ships is the
mission, not the feature.

## Decision

- A mission is a business feature: the unit that ships. It ends in one PR into `main`.
- Milestones are internal iterations. Each runs in its own worktree and integrates into
  `mission/<name>`, which carries fast checks only and is never shippable.
- The mission branch dies at the merge.
- CI red on the PR reopens the mission on its branch (`fix` cycle); it never opens a new PR.
- On the board: cards are milestones, the lane-8 gate group is the mission PR.

## Alternatives

- One PR per feature: more gates, more waiting-on-merge waste, and features inside a
  milestone are not independently shippable anyway.
- Long-lived integration branch (`dev`): rejected; the mission branch's death at merge is
  what prevents it.

## Consequences

PRD v0.2 §2, §8, FR-G; `.github/workflows/mission-branch.yml` targets `mission/**`;
`gate.yml` targets PRs to `main`; the `main` ruleset (D-007) requires a PR.
EOF

# D-002: Tauri 2 + Leptos, with an explicit go/no-go at M1

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted (provisional until M1)

## Context

Constraint: Rust. Preference: Tauri 2. The hard part is `observatory-core` (ingest,
mapping, metrics), not the UI. Rich content (markdown findings, QA video, PR rendering)
needs a webview.

## Decision

Tauri 2 shell with a Leptos (CSR, Trunk) frontend; core logic in a UI-free crate behind
Tauri commands with serde types shared end to end.

Go/no-go at M1 completion: the board renders the M0 replay (nine lanes, correct card

command. If either fails, the frontend switches to Tauri 2 + TypeScript (Svelte) from M2,
`observatory-core` unchanged.

Tauri 2 + Dioxus (same risks, blurs "why Tauri"); Tauri 2 + TypeScript (two languages,
richest UI ecosystem: the fallback); iced and egui (weak for text-heavy Details).

# D-003: Two workflows, one required check, jobs that activate with the code

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted

## Context

RULES.md rule 6 splits CI into light checks on the mission branch (under three minutes
warm) and a full attested run on the one PR into `main`. The `main` ruleset must name
required checks before any code exists, and a required check that never reports hangs the
final PR.

## Decision

- `mission-branch.yml` (on `mission/**`, also `workflow_call`): docs, links, workflows,
  secrets, rust, deny. Aggregate job **`mission-checks`**.
- `gate.yml` (on PRs to `main`): reuses the light workflow, adds Semgrep, Trivy fs, Checkov
  on the workflows, SBOM (syft), macOS Tauri bundle with `attest-build-provenance` and
  cosign keyless signatures. Aggregate job **`gate`**, the only check the ruleset requires.
- Aggregate jobs run `if: always()` and fail on any `failure`/`cancelled` in `needs`;
  skipped jobs count as not applicable. New jobs are added to `needs`, never to the ruleset.
- Rust, fixtures and Tauri jobs are gated by a `detect` job probing for `Cargo.toml`,
  `fixtures/streams/*.jsonl`, and `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`.
- Every action is pinned to a commit digest with a version comment; Renovate keeps them
  current (D-005). Versions verified against GitHub releases on 2026-10-22.
- Workflows call `make` targets so README commands and CI commands are the same thing.

## Alternatives

Listing each job as a required check: brittle, breaks when jobs are renamed or skipped.
Separate workflows per tool: more files, no shared `detect`.

## Consequences

The ruleset (D-007) requires exactly `gate`. The mission must keep the probed paths.
EOF

# D-004: Grafana Cloud over OTLP as the telemetry backend

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted (contract now, code in the mission)

## Context

The PRD needs two kinds of telemetry: the observatory's own traces and metrics (to debug
the app) and the lane-9 mission series (cycle time, waste, tokens, cost) so they can be
charted and alerted on outside the desktop window. The owner provides a Grafana Cloud stack.

## Decision

- Export via OpenTelemetry OTLP (`http/protobuf`) to the stack's OTLP gateway. Endpoint and
  `Authorization: Basic base64(instanceId:token)` come from `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` /
  `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` or the keychain entry `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`.
  Never from the repository.
- Off by default (`[telemetry].enabled = false`); the app must work fully offline.
- App telemetry: `tracing` + `tracing-opentelemetry` spans for ingest, mapping, metrics,
  control; errors as span events (no separate error tracker in v1, see B-003).
- Mission metrics (names are the contract, attributes in parentheses):
  - `observatory.mission.cycle_seconds` (mission, status)
  - `observatory.feature.cycle_seconds` (mission, milestone, feature)
  - `observatory.waste_seconds` (mission, milestone, feature, role, cause)
  - `observatory.rework_windows` (mission, feature, cause, resolved)
  - `observatory.fix_loops` (mission, milestone)
  - `observatory.tokens` (mission, session, role, model, class)
  - `observatory.cost` (mission, role, model, unit, price_table)
  - `observatory.active_agents` (mission, role)
- Resource attributes: `service.name=droid-observatory`, `deployment.environment`,
  `service.namespace`, `service.version`.
- CI telemetry (workflow durations, test timings) is documented only: B-002.

## Alternatives

Prometheus pull (no stable endpoint from a desktop app); Sentry for errors (second vendor;
revisit if span events prove insufficient); no export (loses the external budget meter).

## Consequences

`config/observatory.example.toml` `[telemetry]`, `.env.example`, PRD v0.3 §11.4. GitHub
Actions secret `GRAFANA_OTLP_HEADERS` and variable `GRAFANA_OTLP_ENDPOINT` are reserved
names for B-002.
EOF
// @input: d005 <<'EOF'
# D-005: Renovate with a 7-day minimum release age

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted

## Context

Rule 3 wants versions verified and current; the readiness criterion "minimum dependency
release age" wants a delay before adopting new releases, which cuts exposure to
compromised or quickly-yanked releases.

## Decision

Renovate (`renovate.json`): `minimumReleaseAge: 7 days`, `internalChecksFilter: strict`,
Cargo updates grouped in one PR, GitHub Actions grouped with digests pinned, the Rust
toolchain tracked but labelled `type:decision` (a toolchain bump is a decision file),
security advisories bypass the delay. Weekly schedule, dashboard on.

## Alternatives

Dependabot with `cooldown`: works, but weaker grouping for Cargo and no digest pinning
helper. 14 days: safer, slower; 7 is the common compromise and can be raised by editing
one key.

## Consequences

Renovate must be installed on the repository (GitHub App) by the owner; until then the
config is inert. PRs land on `main` through the normal gate.
EOF

# D-006: Models per role for the mission

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted

## Context

Rule 19: orchestrator, worker and validator models are declared in the spec and the
mission command; a change is a decision file. The owner set the roles on 2026-10-22.

## Decision

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5-1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny and user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Declared in `.factory/settings.json` (`missionOrchestratorModel`,
`missionModelSettings.workerModel`, `missionModelSettings.validationWorkerModel`), the
README mission command, `config/observatory.example.toml` `[mission]`, and the price table
`config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`. Reasoning effort per role is set in `SPEC.md` §2.

## Alternatives

Same model for all roles (simpler, loses the cost/quality split the observatory is meant
to measure); cheaper validators (validation is where correctness is bought).

## Consequences

Lane 9 compares roles across these three models from the first mission. Changing any of
them: new decision file, update the four places above.
EOF
// @input: d007 <<'EOF'
# D-007: Ruleset on main

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted

## Context

`main` is the gate the observatory watches. Its rules must be the ones the PRD's merge
policy reader (FR-G4) will find, and they must not hang the final PR.

## Decision

GitHub ruleset `main-gate`, enforcement active, target `refs/heads/main`:

- pull request required, **required approving reviews: 0** (the human merges by hand; the
  gate is the review), dismiss stale reviews on push, conversation resolution not required;
- required status check: **`gate`** (from `gate.yml`), strict (branch up to date);
- deletion blocked, non-fast-forward (force push) blocked;
- no bypass actors: admins included.

## Alternatives

Legacy branch protection (superseded by rulesets); admin bypass for the first PR (would
let the readiness PR skip the gate it introduces); requiring every job by name (D-003).

## Consequences

Applied with `gh api` on 2026-10-22 and recorded in `ai/session/`. Direct pushes to `main`
fail for everyone, including the owner; `.githooks/pre-push` and
`.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` refuse them earlier.
EOF

README mission command, `config/observatory.example.toml` `[mission]`, and the price table
`config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`. Reasoning effort per role is set in `SPEC.md` §2.

## Alternatives

Same model for all roles (simpler, loses the cost/quality split the observatory is meant
to measure); cheaper validators (validation is where correctness is bought).

## Consequences

Lane 9 compares roles across these three models from the first mission. Changing any of
them: new decision file, update the four places above.

# D-007: Ruleset on main

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted

## Context

`main` is the gate the observatory watches. Its rules must be the ones the PRD's merge
policy reader (FR-G4) will find, and they must not hang the final PR.

## Decision

GitHub ruleset `main-gate`, enforcement active, target `refs/heads/main`:

- pull request required, **required approving reviews: 0** (the human merges by hand; the
  gate is the review), dismiss stale reviews on push, conversation resolution not required;
- required status check: **`gate`** (from `gate.yml`), strict (branch up to date);
- deletion blocked, non-fast-forward (force push) blocked;
- no bypass actors: admins included.

## Alternatives

Legacy branch protection (superseded by rulesets); admin bypass for the first PR (would
let the readiness PR skip the gate it introduces); requiring every job by name (D-003).

## Consequences

Applied with `gh api` on 2026-10-22 and recorded in `ai/session/`. Direct pushes to `main`
fail for everyone, including the owner; `.githooks/pre-push` and
`.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` refuse them earlier.

# Backlog

Deferred items with their reasons (ai/RULES.md rule 14). Reference as `B-NNN` from code
(`TODO(B-NNN)`) and decisions. Scheduled items move to the spec; dropped items stay here with
the reason struck through, not deleted.

| Id | Item | Reason deferred | Earliest |
|---|---|---|---|
| B-001 | Devcontainer for Linux CI parity | Tauri on macOS is the target; a container cannot run the window. Useful for core-only work. | after skeleton |
| B-002 | CI telemetry to Grafana (workflow durations, test timings) via OTLP | Owner: document only for now. Secret `GRAFANA_OTLP_HEADERS`, variable `GRAFANA_OTLP_ENDPOINT` reserved. | after M5 |
| B-003 | Dedicated error tracking (Sentry or Grafana Faro) | D-004 uses span events first; add a tracker only if they prove insufficient. | after M2 |
| B-004 | Release notes automation (git-cliff from conventional-ish subjects) | No releases until the mission PR; one PR means one changelog entry. | at first release |
| B-005 | Coverage thresholds (`cargo-llvm-cov`, fail under a stated %) | Needs code; the number needs a reason. Spec §6 to set it. | with skeleton |
| B-006 | Log scrubbing utility for raw JSONL rendering | PRD renders raw lines read-only; a redaction pass before display is the next step. | M1 |
| B-007 | Private demo repository with PR flow, CI and rulesets for M4 | Needed before M4 starts; owner creates it. | before M4 |
| B-008 | Human-computed reference spreadsheet from the M0 capture for M5 | Mission input; cannot be produced by validators. | before M5 |
| B-009 | Optional manual ~20-minute mission capture before the mission starts | Insurance for M0 planning, not structural. | before mission |
| B-010 | Settle walking-skeleton vs M0 boundary in SPEC.md | Rule 2 and PRD §13 overlap; the spec session decides order. | spec session |
| B-011 | Fill `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml` from the vendor price page, set `verified = true` | Prices must be read on the day, not recalled. | before M5 |
| B-012 | Runbook: stalled mission, red gate, fix cycle, hooks disabled | Needs the app to exist to describe recovery honestly. | M3 |
| B-013 | GitHub code scanning default setup (CodeQL) | Enabled if the API accepts Rust for this repo; otherwise Semgrep in the gate covers SAST. | now / M1 |
| B-014 | Dead code and unused dependency checks (`cargo-udeps`, `cargo-machete`) in the mission-branch CI | Needs code; nightly toolchain for udeps is a cost to weigh. Spec §7 decides. | with skeleton |
| B-015 | Readiness report re-run at every milestone integration, stored in `reports/readiness/` | Baseline exists; cadence belongs to the spec. | each milestone |

# reports

Numbers pasted from the tools that produced them (ai/RULES.md rule 7).

- `readiness/<date>-<label>.json`: Agent Readiness reports (`/readiness-report`). Baseline
  `2026-10-22-baseline.json`: Level 1, 5 of 65 evaluated criteria.
- `usage/<milestone>.md`: tokens per role and model, waste by cause, wall time, per
  integrated milestone (written by the orchestrator at integration).

input.old_str: ## 12. Technology options and recommendation
input.new_str:
### 11.4 Telemetry export (Grafana Cloud)

Two kinds of telemetry leave the app, both over OpenTelemetry OTLP (`http/protobuf`) to a Grafana Cloud stack, both off by default so the app works fully offline (decision D-004):

- **App telemetry**: `tracing` spans for ingest, mapping, metrics, and control; errors as span events.
- **Mission metrics**: the lane-9 series, so the budget meter and waste can be charted and alerted on outside the desktop window. Metric names are a contract: `observatory.mission.cycle_seconds`, `observatory.feature.cycle_seconds`, `observatory.waste_seconds` (by role and cause), `observatory.rework_windows`, `observatory.fix_loops`, `observatory.tokens` (by role, model, class), `observatory.cost` (by unit and price table), `observatory.active_agents`.

Endpoint and credentials come from `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` / `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` or the OS keychain, never from the repository. Config keys and defaults: `config/observatory.example.toml` `[telemetry]`. CI telemetry is deferred (B-002).
## 12. Technology options and recommendation

const root = '/Users/dct/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory';
// @input: todos <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Every TODO or FIXME marker in source files must point at an issue (#123) or a
# backlog item (B-123) so debt is tracked, not scattered (ai/RULES.md rule 14).
# Prose (markdown), data (json, jsonl) and logs are not scanned: they talk about
# markers without being one.
set -eu
pattern='(TODO|FIXME)'
ok='(TODO|FIXME)\((#[0-9]+|B-[0-9]+)\)'
status=0
files=$(git ls-files \
  | grep -E '(\.(rs|toml|ya?ml|sh|js|ts|tsx|html|css|scss|sql|py)$|^Makefile$|^\.githooks/|^\.factory/hooks/)' \
  | grep -Ev '^(build-log/|fixtures/|scripts/check-todos\.sh$)')
for f in $files; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  hits=$(grep -nE "$pattern" "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -vE "$ok" || true)
  if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$hits" | sed "s|^|$f:|"
    echo "  -> write TODO(#issue) or TODO(B-nnn)"
    status=1
  fi
done
exit $status

#!/bin/sh
# Every TODO or FIXME marker in source files must point at an issue (#123) or a
# backlog item (B-123) so debt is tracked, not scattered (ai/RULES.md rule 14).
# Prose (markdown), data (json, jsonl) and logs are not scanned: they talk about
# markers without being one.
set -eu
pattern='(TODO|FIXME)'
ok='(TODO|FIXME)\((#[0-9]+|B-[0-9]+)\)'
status=0
files=$(git ls-files \
  | grep -E '(\.(rs|toml|ya?ml|sh|js|ts|tsx|html|css|scss|sql|py)$|^Makefile$|^\.githooks/|^\.factory/hooks/)' \
  | grep -Ev '^(build-log/|fixtures/|scripts/check-todos\.sh$)')
for f in $files; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  hits=$(grep -nE "$pattern" "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -vE "$ok" || true)
  if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$hits" | sed "s|^|$f:|"
    echo "  -> write TODO(#issue) or TODO(B-nnn)"
    status=1
  fi
done
exit $status

No PRs are merged yet, and fast_ci_feedback criterion technically depends on merged PRs, which creates ambiguity. I still need to pull check durations and ruleset info, and resolve dependency_update_automation — Renovate config exists but the app isn't installed yet, so I should pass this with a caveat rather than treat it as fully satisfied.

Going through the repository criteria one by one: large_file_detection, tech_debt_tracking, build_cmd_doc, and vcs_cli_tools all pass; deps_pinned fails since there's no package manifest despite pinned actions/toolchain; automated_pr_review fails for lack of review-content generation; agentic_development and fast_ci_feedback both pass given the fast gate runtime.

Continuing down the list, build_performance_tracking, deployment_frequency, feature_flag_infrastructure, release_notes_automation, and release_automation all fail since there's no tracking, deploy pipeline, or flag system in place. Single_command_setup I'll pass since README documents a clean-clone sequence to the runnable `make check` target, and agents_md, readme, and automated_doc_generation (via the decisions index script) all pass too.

Moving on, skills fails, documentation_freshness and service_flow_documented pass, agents_md_validation passes indirectly since CI runs the same make targets AGENTS.md documents, devcontainer fails, env_template passes via .env.example, runbooks_documented fails, branch_protection passes via the main-gate ruleset, and I'm now checking secret scanning.

For secret scanning gitleaks is present so I'll pass that, and codeowners also passes. For automated_security_review I'm weighing whether the Trivy SARIF artifact counts as a readable report — it's uploaded as an artifact but not surfaced in the PR itself, so I'm leaning toward being conservative and marking this one as failing.

I'm going through the rest of the checklist: dependency update automation passes via renovate config, gitignore and secrets management both pass given the env file handling and secret references, release age, issue templates, labeling, and PR templates all pass, while backlog health fails since it's about GitHub issues rather than the markdown file. Now I'm moving into the application-level criteria, starting with lint config, which looks like it should pass based on the clippy config, Makefile, and CI setup, though I need to check if a Cargo.toml exists.

Lint config and formatter config both pass since clippy and rustfmt are properly set up, but type checking is trickier since there's no actual code to compile yet -- I'm leaning toward failing that one since no build has actually been invoked.

For the other checks: pre-commit hooks pass, naming consistency passes since AGENTS.md documents conventions, and cyclomatic complexity is ambiguous since clippy's cognitive-complexity lint is in the nursery category and isn't enabled by default even though a threshold is configured. I could fix this by explicitly enabling the lint in the Makefile, though that means another commit and CI run.

For dead code detection, RUSTFLAGS with -D warnings in both workflows turns the compiler's default dead_code lint into a build failure, so I'll count that mechanism as configured and passing even without actual code yet. Duplicate code detection and unused dependency detection remain unaddressed for now.

Testing categories all fail since there's no test suite at all—no unit tests, integration tests, performance tracking, flaky test detection, coverage thresholds, or isolation guarantees exist yet, though AGENTS.md at least documents naming conventions. The interactive QA path is only documented for a future app state that doesn't exist yet, so I have to mark that honestly as failing along with structured logging.

Observability is equally absent: no distributed tracing, metrics collection, code quality metrics, error tracking, alerting, or deployment observability, even though some contracts document intentions. Log scrubbing and product analytics also fail outright. I'm now tallying up the passing categories for the repo—large file handling, tech debt tracking, build commands, version control, agentic workflows, fast CI, single command execution, AGENTS.md presence, README, and auto-documentation all count as passes.

Totaling things up, the repo hits 24 of 36 criteria and the app hits 7 of 29, giving an overall 31/65 (47.7%), which lands at Level 3. My plan now is to make the clippy fix, commit and push it to trigger the gate rerun, then check readiness, and finally proceed to merge.

## Repository / identities
- Local repo: `/Users/dct/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`; GitHub `dctellya/droid-observatory` (public). User: David Carbajosa Tesoro (`dct`, GitHub `dctellya`), admin on repo; `gh` authenticated. Droid CLI version 0.247.0. Locale is Spanish for git messages.

- Remote branch `chore/repo-readiness` still exists (merged; could be deleted).

## Standing user instructions (preserve)
1. **Log every interaction of this session under `ai/session/`** — running log is `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md`, entries 1–13 so far, numbered `## Entry N — <title>` with request (verbatim), context, actions, decisions. Keep appending for every new user message/action.
2. Follow `ai/RULES.md` (19 rules, user-authored): tests before code; walking skeleton first; versions verified+dated; no secrets/magic values; clean-clone commands = CI commands; CI gate split (light on `mission/<name>`, full attested on the single PR to `main`); counts pasted from tools; **git forward only (never amend/reset/rebase/stash/force-push), one PR per mission, nothing reaches `main` except via PR**; one file per decision in `docs/decisions/`; human intervenes only at milestone boundaries; everything logged; unknown events surfaced; models per role declared.
3. Spec generation must follow `ai/SPEC-TEMPLATE.md` (user-authored).
4. Models per role (user decision): orchestrator `claude-fable-5-1`, workers `claude-sonnet-5-5`, validators `claude-opus-5-5`.
5. Commit trailer used for agent commits: `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`. Commit subjects ≤72 chars (commit-msg hook enforces).

## Work completed
### PRD (`ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`, now v0.3)
- Rust desktop app (Tauri 2 + Leptos recommended, M1 go/no-go: ≤3 worker sessions of rework after first scrutiny + clean Trunk build; fallback Tauri+TypeScript). Hosts missions via `droid exec --mission --output-format stream-jsonrpc` and reads `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/<id>.jsonl`; lane = view over raw JSONL, not a copy.
- Nine lanes (user-defined, verbatim in PRD §7): Intent, Orchestrator, Workers, Validators-scrutiny, Validators-user-testing, Integration, Human, Outside, Time/Waste/Cost/models.
- Delivery model (user review, D-001): mission = shippable business feature = one PR into `main`; milestones = internal iterations in worktrees integrated into `mission/<name>` (dies at merge); **card = milestone** (features inside); lane 8 = one gate group per mission PR; CI red reopens mission on its branch (`fix` cycle), same PR.
- Metrics: time states (active, waiting on human incl. waiting-on-merge sub-cause, waiting on validation, retry/failure, idle-queued vs idle-unscheduled); bounded rework windows (signal→resolution, overlapping merge); first-pass = active outside windows; mission overhead reported separately; cycle time feature/milestone/mission (mission ends at `pr.merged` with CI green); cost via Factory credits if exposed else dated price table (`config/prices/<date>.toml`). User agreed on both v0.2 call-outs.
- v0.3 added §11.4 telemetry (Grafana Cloud OTLP) and models per role; Appendix C has changelog.

<coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec (when written): `SPEC.md`.

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; load the same fixture from the launch screen; the nine
   lanes render and a card opens its Details view.

No login gate: the app reads local files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to `BACKLOG.md` as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs or issues.
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5-1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission". Reasoning effort per role is set in `SPEC.md`.
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

317→
318→- **The lane is a view, not a copy.** The store indexes events with a pointer to the raw JSONL line (file, byte offset). Opening an event in the UI reads the raw line on demand.
319→- `observatory-core` has no UI dependency and is testable from fixtures (recorded mission streams). A thin CLI (`observatory replay <session>`) exercises it headlessly and is the first thing that works.
320→- The GitHub adapter is behind a trait so other forges and CI systems can follow.
321→
322→### 11.3 Security
323→
324→- GitHub token and Factory credentials stay in the OS keychain (Tauri keyring plugin). Never written to the store or logs.
325→- Raw JSONL may contain secrets from tool output; the app renders it read-only and never uploads it.
326→- Merge is the only outward-facing write. It requires an explicit confirmation naming the PR and target branch.
327→
328→### 11.4 Telemetry export (Grafana Cloud)
329→
330→Two kinds of telemetry leave the app, both over OpenTelemetry OTLP (`http/protobuf`) to a Grafana Cloud stack, both off by default so the app works fully offline (decision D-004):
331→
332→- **App telemetry**: `tracing` spans for ingest, mapping, metrics, and control; errors as span events.
333→- **Mission metrics**: the lane-9 series, so the budget meter and waste can be charted and alerted on outside the desktop window. Metric names are a contract: `observatory.mission.cycle_seconds`, `observatory.feature.cycle_seconds`, `observatory.waste_seconds` (by role and cause), `observatory.rework_windows`, `observatory.fix_loops`, `observatory.tokens` (by role, model, class), `observatory.cost` (by unit and price table), `observatory.active_agents`.
334→
335→Endpoint and credentials come from `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` / `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` or the OS keychain, never from the repository. Config keys and defaults: `config/observatory.example.toml` `[telemetry]`. CI telemetry is deferred (B-002).
336→
337→## 12. Technology options and recommendation
338→
339→Constraint: Rust. Preference: Tauri 2. Needs: data-dense board, live updates, charts, markdown and video rendering in Details, long-lived subprocess management, SQLite.
340→
341→| Option | Pros | Cons |
342→|---|---|---|
343→| **A. Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust, CSR via Trunk)** | Single language; shared serde types between core and UI with no bindings; fine-grained reactivity suits a live board; webview gives markdown, video, CSS layout for free. | Charting ecosystem thinner than JS; WASM/Trunk toolchain adds build steps; smaller community. **Droids have far less Leptos in their training than React or Svelte**, so worker rework on UI tasks is likely higher. **The WASM/Trunk toolchain inside a Mission is a new failure mode** (toolchain install, target, dev server) that validators may struggle to diagnose. |
344→| B. Tauri 2 + Dioxus | Same single-language benefit; React-like ergonomics; growing fast. | Dioxus also ships its own desktop renderer, which blurs the "why Tauri" story; same training-data and toolchain concerns as A. |
345→| C. Tauri 2 + TypeScript (Svelte or React) | Richest charting and UI libraries; fastest to a polished UI; best-known stack for Droids. | Two languages; types must be generated (ts-rs/specta) and kept in sync; the user's stated preference is Rust. |
346→| D. iced (native) | Pure Rust, no webview, small binary, Elm architecture fits an event-driven board. | Markdown, video, and rich text are weak; complex layouts cost more effort; no Tauri plugin ecosystem (keyring, updater, tray). |
347→| E. egui (native, immediate mode) | Trivial live updates and plots (egui_plot); excellent for dashboards. | Looks like a tool, not an app; text-heavy Details view (review notes, markdown) is awkward; accessibility and theming limited. |
348→
349→**Recommendation: Option A, Tauri 2 + Leptos, with M1 as an explicit go/no-go.**
350→
351→Reasoning: the hard part of this product is `observatory-core` (ingest, mapping, metrics), not the UI. Keeping the UI in Rust means the metric types, lane mapping, and event model are used directly in the view with no translation layer, which is where drift and bugs would otherwise appear. The webview covers the rich-content needs (markdown findings, QA video, PR rendering) that native options handle poorly. Charting is the one real gap; lane 9 needs stacked bars and timelines, achievable as SVG from Leptos signals, with a JS chart library as a documented escape hatch.
352→
353→**Go/no-go criterion (evaluated at M1 completion):** the board renders the M0 replay (all nine lanes, cards positioned correctly, Details timeline open) with **at most 3 worker sessions of rework** after the first scrutiny pass, and the Trunk/WASM build succeeds from a clean checkout with the documented command. If either fails, switch to Option C for M2 onward, keeping `observatory-core` unchanged; the Tauri command boundary is designed to make that swap possible. (Threshold of 3 agreed 2026-10-22; may be adjusted at planning time.)
354→
355→## 13. Milestones (seed of the mission plan)
356→
357→**One mission, six milestones, one branch `mission/observatory-v1`, one PR at the end.** Each milestone runs in its own worktree and integrates into the mission branch with fast checks. M0 must complete before the orchestrator plans M1 onward in detail, because the stream schema is unknown until the capture exists.
358→
359→| # | Name | Outcome | Validation |
360→|---|---|---|---|
361→| M0 | Stream capture and mapping | Capture one real mission run (`droid exec --mission` on a sample repo); write the raw→lane event mapper with fixtures; `observatory replay` CLI prints lane events. Freeze the mapping, versioned by Droid version. | Fixture tests pass; `unknown.event` count on the capture is zero; every event kind in section 7 that appears in the capture is mapped. **Gate for planning M1–M5 in detail.** |
362→| M1 | Board in replay | Tauri 2 + Leptos app renders the nine lanes and milestone cards from JSONL replay; Details timeline tab; scrubber; unmapped tray. | Replay of the M0 capture shows all milestones and features with correct lane positions versus the capture's known outcome. **Leptos go/no-go evaluated here (section 12).** |
363→| M2 | Live host and agents | Launch screen; spawn `droid exec --mission`; live board; agent panel with current agent per feature; live output per agent; `model.changed` and `context.compacted` markers. | A live mission shows events within 1 s; agent attribution matches orchestrator logs. |
364→| M3 | Intervention | Pause/resume, message, answer/approve/deny, mark complete/skipped; stall flag with suggested prompts. | Each action produces a lane 7 event and the orchestrator reacts. |
365→| M4 | Mission branch, gate, and fix loop | Git adapter (mission branch, worktrees, fast checks → lane 6); GitHub adapter; gate group in lane 8; gate badge; merge policy with rule attribution; Merge button; CI red → `fix` cycle on the affected card, same PR. | Tested against a **private demo repository with a PR flow, CI, and rulesets** (the observatory itself has no PR flow until the end of the mission). A red check on the demo PR opens a fix cycle; a green check with human policy shows Merge; merging via the app updates the badge. |
366→| M5 | Time, waste, cost | Time-state engine; rework windows; mission overhead; cycle, waste, bottleneck; tokens per sub-droid; dated price table; budget meter; model comparison; CSV/JSON export. | Metrics recomputed from the M0 capture match a **human-produced reference spreadsheet** computed by hand once from the same capture, within rounding. The spreadsheet is a mission input, not something validators invent. |
367→
368→Optional insurance before the mission starts: a manual ~20-minute capture of a small mission, so the orchestrator has something to look at while planning M0. It is not a structural step.
369→
370→Dogfooding: from M1 onward the mission that builds the observatory is observed in the observatory. Its own lane 8 stays empty until the final PR `mission/observatory-v1` → `main`.
371→
372→## 14. Risks and open questions
373→
374→| Risk / question | Mitigation |
375→|---|---|
376→| Mission JSON-RPC event schema is not fully documented; mapping to features, milestones, and validator roles may be heuristic. | M0 captures and freezes a versioned mapping with fixtures; `unknown.event` is counted and shown, never dropped; M0 is the gate before detailed planning. |
377→| Leptos: less Droid training data than React/Svelte; WASM/Trunk toolchain is a new failure mode inside a mission. | Core first and headless; M1 go/no-go with a written criterion; swap to TypeScript at the Tauri command boundary. |
378→| Factory Standard Credits may not be exposed per session in the stream. | Price table fallback is first-class; the UI always names the unit and the price-table date. |
379→| Attestation formats vary (GitHub artifact attestations, SLSA provenance, custom). | v1 reads GitHub artifact attestations and check-run conclusions (`attestation.recorded`), verifies via GitHub's attestation API where possible (`attestation.verified`); others appear as opaque recorded events with a link. |
380→| Merge policy lives in several places (branch protection, rulesets, CODEOWNERS, org policy). | v1 reads branch protection and rulesets, plus an explicit app-level override per repo; the Details gate tab shows which rule decided. |
381→| A `fix` cycle after the orchestrator has ended needs a follow-up mission with the right context on the same branch. | The fix launch pre-fills the mission file with the feature spec, the failing check output, the mission branch, and the original session ids. |
382→| Local JSONL files may change format between Droid versions. | The mapper is versioned by the Droid version observed in the session settings file; replay of old captures stays in the test suite. |
383→| M4 cannot be tested on the observatory repo itself. | Private demo repository with PR flow, CI, and rulesets, prepared before M4. |
384→| M5 has no oracle unless a human produces one. | Reference spreadsheet from the M0 capture is a listed mission input. |
385→| Webview charting in Rust is thinner than JS. | Scoped chart set (stacked bars, timeline, sparkline) built as SVG components; JS chart lib as a documented escape hatch. |
386→
387→## 15. Acceptance criteria for this PRD
388→
389→The PRD is accepted when the reviewer agrees that:
390→
391→1. The delivery model (mission = shippable business feature, milestones = internal iterations on `mission/<name>`, one PR) is stated correctly.
392→2. The nine lanes, their sources, and their event kinds are correct and complete, with `unknown.event` as a first-class kind.
393→3. Card = milestone, features inside the card, one gate group per mission PR, and the fix loop reopening the mission on its branch match the intended workflow.
394→4. The time states, bounded rework windows, first-pass definition, mission overhead, waiting on merge, and the queued/unscheduled idle split are the ones to measure against.
395→5. Hosting plus local-file ingest plus git and GitHub adapters is the right v1 data source set.
396→6. The stack recommendation (Tauri 2 + Leptos) with the M1 go/no-go criterion is approved, or a different option is chosen.
397→7. The milestone plan (M0 as planning gate, demo repo for M4, human reference for M5) is acceptable as the seed of the mission plan.

# D-002: Tauri 2 + Leptos, with an explicit go/no-go at M1

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted (provisional until M1)

## Context

Constraint: Rust. Preference: Tauri 2. The hard part is `observatory-core` (ingest,
mapping, metrics), not the UI. Rich content (markdown findings, QA video, PR rendering)
needs a webview.

## Decision

Tauri 2 shell with a Leptos (CSR, Trunk) frontend; core logic in a UI-free crate behind
Tauri commands with serde types shared end to end.

Go/no-go at M1 completion: the board renders the M0 replay (nine lanes, correct card
positions, Details timeline) with at most 3 worker sessions of rework after the first
scrutiny pass, and the Trunk/WASM build succeeds from a clean checkout with the documented
command. If either fails, the frontend switches to Tauri 2 + TypeScript (Svelte) from M2,
`observatory-core` unchanged.

## Alternatives

Tauri 2 + Dioxus (same risks, blurs "why Tauri"); Tauri 2 + TypeScript (two languages,
richest UI ecosystem: the fallback); iced and egui (weak for text-heavy Details).

## Consequences

Named risks: less Leptos in Droid training data than React/Svelte; the WASM/Trunk toolchain
inside a mission is a new failure mode. `rust-toolchain.toml` includes
`wasm32-unknown-unknown`; the gate's `bundle` job installs `trunk` and `tauri-cli`.

// @input: decision <<'EOF'
# D-008: Attach is the primary live mode

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted

## Context

Missions are started from the terminal in practice (`droid exec --mission ...` in a
project's directory). Every session, including the child sessions of workers and
validators, is written as it runs to `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/<id>.jsonl`. PRD v0.3
treated hosting (the app spawns `droid exec`) as the live mode and attach as an afterthought,
which made a launch screen a prerequisite for watching anything live (M2) and left the
dogfooding statement ("from M1 onward") without a mechanism.

## Decision

Attach is the primary live mode. The observatory watches `~/.factory/sessions/` with a
filesystem notifier, detects any new session JSONL, tails it as it grows and renders it
within 1 s, named by its `--tag` or session id. Replay is attach at end-of-file: one adapter
(`jsonl_watch` + `jsonl_tail`), one code path. Hosting remains as the secondary path and the
only mode with a control channel (pause, message, answer over the JSON-RPC input stream).

Milestones: attach moves into M1 with replay; M1 acceptance adds "start a mission in a
terminal, see its events on the board within 1 s". M2 becomes hosting only. The agent panel
and the `model.changed` / `context.compacted` markers move to M1 because they are read-only
views over the same events. PRD v0.4, §1, §9.7, §11.1, §11.2, §13, §14, §15.

## Alternatives

- Host first (v0.3): every observed mission must be launched from the app; nothing can be
  watched until the launch screen, process management and RPC plumbing exist.
- Attach by explicit file pick only, no watcher: works, but the user has to find the session
  id for each mission and misses child sessions.

## Consequences

- Dogfooding starts the moment M1 lands: M2–M5 of the mission that builds the observatory
  are watched by attaching to its own session files.
- New risk rows: notifier coalescing or missed events (paired with a poll at
  `[ingest].jsonl_poll_ms` and a startup scan of the directory); `--tag` recoverability
  from the session files (confirmed in M0).
- `config/observatory.example.toml` `[ingest]` gains `watch_sessions_dir`.
- The Leptos go/no-go (D-002) is unchanged: it judges the board rendering, not ingest.

# Session Log: 2026-10-22

**Project:** droid-observatory
**Repo state at start:** `main` at `c830823` (Initial commit) — only `LICENSE` and `README.md` present.
**Purpose of this log:** Record every interaction in this session, including the mission that follows, so the work is traceable.

---

## Entry 1 — Session setup

**User request**

> I want to log all this session under ai/session/
> Including the later interaction of the mission we are going to embarc

**Context gathered**

- `README.md`: "droid observatory to observe how a Business feature progresses across the build lifecycle and maybe the SDCL"
- No `ai/` directory existed yet.

**Actions taken**

- Created `ai/session/` directory.
- Created this file, `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md`, as the running log.

**Convention going forward**

- Each user message and the resulting actions get a numbered entry (`## Entry N — <title>`).
- Each entry records: the user request (verbatim or summarized), context gathered, actions taken, files changed, and any decisions or open questions.
- The mission, once stated, gets its own section below and is updated as work progresses.

---

## Mission

Build **droid-observatory**: a Rust desktop app that visualizes how features move through a Factory mission's orchestrated states, with validation status, review notes, merge control, human intervention, agent attribution, and flow metrics (cycle time, waste, bottlenecks).

**Current phase:** PRD v0.3 accepted; repository readiness in progress on `chore/repo-readiness`; spec session next.

---

## Entry 2 — Mission stated: ideation phase → PRD

**User request (verbatim)**

> Perfect. We are going to start with an ideation phase, the outcome is a PRD that I will review. The intent is to create a droid-observatory for missions, where I want to see how a feature or features evolve thru the engineering building cicle using the default orchestrated states of a mission as lanes. I want the droid observatory to be a desktop app written in rust (my preference is Tauri 2, but I'm open to options), the observatory should show if the feature has been validated and is red or green, also it should show review notes by clicking a details button and if it requires a human merge give us the capability to merge. Also the observatory should allow for human intervention if a feature is not progressing as expected (although this should be the less of the cases when we are on a mission). It should show which agent is working on it at a given point of time. I want to also meassure cycle time, waste and bottlenecks.

**Requirements extracted**

1. Desktop app in Rust; preferred stack Tauri 2 (open to alternatives).
2. Board view: lanes = default orchestrated states of a Factory mission; cards = features.
3. Per feature: validation status (red/green).
4. Per feature: "Details" button → review notes.
5. Per feature: if human merge required → merge action from the app.
6. Human intervention on stalled / off-track features (expected to be rare).
7. Show which agent is currently working on each feature.
8. Metrics: cycle time, waste, bottlenecks.

**Plan for this phase**

1. Research Factory mission model (states, API/CLI surface) from docs.
2. Clarify open decisions with the user where needed.
3. Draft PRD → `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`.
4. Update this log with decisions and outcome.

**Research findings (Factory docs, local machine)**

- Docs name the mission roles (orchestrator, feature workers, validators: *scrutiny* and *user-testing*, milestones) but do **not** publish named feature states. Lanes must be defined by us.
- Public API: `GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/children` (mission agents + last status + attention), `POST .../interrupt`, `POST .../messages`.
- `droid exec --mission --output-format stream-jsonrpc` exposes a live JSON-RPC event stream (text deltas, tool events, token usage). Richest data; app must host the mission.
- No mission has run on this machine; `~/.factory` has no mission data to inspect. Sessions are stored as `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl`.

**Decisions (user, via questionnaire)**

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Data source | Host missions (spawn `droid exec --mission`, consume JSON-RPC stream) **and** read local `~/.factory` session files |
| Lanes | User will provide the exact list of states |
| Merge | Merge = the **gate**: feature PR into `main`, by human or policy, triggering attested CI (and CD if part of an ecosystem). Work inside the mission is integration, not the gate |
| UI stack | Compare options in PRD and recommend one |

---

## Entry 3 — Added requirement: mission cost

**User request (verbatim)**

> Also I would like to meassure cost of the mission, by meassuring token usage per sub-droid

**Requirement added**

9. Cost: measure token usage (and derived cost) per sub-droid (orchestrator, each worker, each validator), aggregated per feature, per milestone, and per mission.

**Open questions still pending**

- Exact ordered list of mission states (lanes).
- How the external merge gate appears on the board (final lane, badge, or both).
- Card granularity (mission feature vs feature PR).

---

## Entry 4 — Final design decisions before PRD draft

**Decisions (user, via questionnaire)**

**Lanes (exact, ordered):**

1. **Intent**: mission prompt, spec, acceptance criteria; later human re-prompts. Few events.
2. **Orchestrator**: plan, feature breakdown, milestones, task assignment, replans.
3. **Workers**: one sub-lane per worker (or per feature when the mission names them); events: task started, files touched, tests run, commits, task done.
4. **Validators, scrutiny**: review findings, blocking vs non-blocking, re-work requested.
5. **Validators, user testing**: QA runs against the built thing, scenario results.
6. **Integration**: worktree merges into the mission branch, conflicts, gate command runs ("integrated in mission", not "merged").
7. **Human**: approvals, answers to escalations, review of the outcome (the video), the merge of the PR.
8. **Outside**: GitHub PR opened, CI runs and attestations, deploys (ecosystem lane; empty for the observatory itself).
9. **Time, Waste, Cost and models**: tokens and usage per role, which model did what; doubles as budget meter; elapsed time, time stuck/wasted.

Every event carries session id, role, model, timestamp, duration, and a link to the raw JSONL line. **The lane is a view, not a copy.** Lanes 1–6 from the stream, 7–8 from GitHub and human actions, 9 from session metadata.

**Waste definition (user):**
- Active time: worker/validator/orchestrator doing something (tool call in flight, model generating).
- Waiting on human: question/approval open, nobody acting (lane 7 open, lanes 2–6 idle).
- Waiting on validation: work done, validator not started.
- Rework: time spent after a blocking finding on the same task.
- Retry and failure: tool errors, re-runs of same command, integration conflicts.
- **Waste = everything that is not active time on first-pass work**, split by cause, per feature and per role. Cost shown next to it (tokens × per-model multiplier) so slow-cheap vs fast-expensive models compare honestly.

**Gate (lane 8 + badge):** final lane holds the gate (PR opened → checks → merged); card badge shows gate state (pending, human required, policy-merged, CI green/red). **CI red reopens the mission**: new mission cycle on the same feature tagged `fix`, drawn as a loop back into Workers lane. Merge button appears only when policy says a human merges; otherwise badge flips to policy-merged automatically. A mission is complete when the gate is green and the merge happened, not when workers stop. Every red is a counted rework loop in lane 9.

**Card:** one card = one mission feature. Gate lane groups cards by the PR that carries them, badge on the group. A PR with three features shows three cards sharing one gate state. CI red loops back only to the card the fix touches.

## Entry 6 — User review of PRD v0.1

**User review notes (verbatim)**

> # Review notes on droid-observatory-prd.md (22-oct-2026)
>
> Hints on the four points raised, plus one model correction that changes sections 7 and 12.
>
> ## 0. Delivery model (overrides my earlier "one milestone = one PR")
>
> - A **mission is a business feature: the unit that ships.** For this project, v1 of the observatory. One PR into `main` at the end, outcome-sized, with the evidence attached; the full attested CI runs on that PR; CD runs from `main`.
> - **Milestones are internal iterations**, not shippable. Each runs in its own worktree and is integrated into a `mission/<name>` branch, the mission's interface to `main`. Fast checks run on that branch (tests, lint, the gate command) to keep it healthy; nothing on it is shippable or pretends to be.
> - The mission branch is short-lived by construction: it dies at the merge. That is what keeps it from becoming git-flow's `dev`.
> - The board agrees with this: cards are milestones (the spec phases); the gate group is the mission's one PR; lane 6 is integration into `mission/<name>`; lane 8 is the PR. The fix loop after CI red reopens the mission on its branch; it does not open a new PR.
> - M0 (stream capture and mapping) is the first milestone of the same mission: the orchestrator captures a run and freezes the mapping before planning the rest. A manual 20-minute capture beforehand is optional insurance, not a structural step.
>
> ## 1. Section 6, event kinds to add
>
> - Lane 1 (Intent): `question.asked` (orchestrator to human), `intent.answered`, `spec.versioned`.
> - Lane 2 (Orchestrator): `milestone.completed`, `task.skipped`, `mission.paused`, `mission.resumed`, `mission.completed`, `context.compacted` (explains sudden quality drops).
> - Lane 3 (Workers): `subagent.spawned`, `subagent.finished`, `permission.requested`, `permission.granted`, `permission.denied`, `hook.blocked` (the write guard), `usage.reported` (feeds lane 9), `model.changed`.
> - Lane 4 (Scrutiny): `rework.resolved`, the closing event that bounds a rework window.
> - Lane 6 (Integration): `gate_command.passed` and `gate_command.failed`, not only `run`.
> - Lane 8 (Outside): `pr.review_requested`, `check.required_missing`, `ruleset.blocked`, `attestation.verified` (distinct from `attestation.recorded`).
> - Keep `unknown.event` as a first-class kind, counted and surfaced; M0's exit criterion is driving it to zero on the capture.
>
> ## 2. Section 9.2, metric definitions
>
> - **Rework** as written counts all active time after the first blocking signal, so legitimate new work after a fix reads as waste. Bound it: rework = active time between a blocking signal (`finding.blocking`, `qa.scenario.failed`, `integration.conflict`, `check.failed`) and its resolution event (`rework.resolved`, `qa.scenario.passed`, conflict resolved, `check.passed`), per signal. Overlapping windows merge.
> - **First-pass active time** = active time outside any rework window (not "before the first blocking signal").
> - **Mission overhead**: orchestrator time before `feature.defined` (and replanning time not attributable to one feature) belongs to no card. Report it separately, or apportion it explicitly; otherwise feature cycle times look shorter than the mission.
> - **Waiting on merge**: checks green, policy requires a human, nobody has merged. Add it as its own cause under waiting on human; it will be the largest waste bucket in practice.
> - **Cycle time** stops at `pr.merged` (human or policy) with CI green: correct for the gate.
> - **Idle** should distinguish "queued behind another feature" (WIP limit) from "nothing scheduled"; the first is a bottleneck signal, the second is not.
>
> ## 3. Section 11, stack
>
> - Tauri 2 + Leptos is defensible for the stated needs (markdown and video in Details, shared serde types, live board).
> - Two risks to name: Droids have far less Leptos than React or Svelte in their training, and the WASM/Trunk toolchain inside a Mission is a new failure mode. Mitigations already in the PRD are the right ones (core first, headless `observatory replay`, swap to TypeScript at the Tauri command boundary); make M1 the explicit go/no-go on Leptos, with the criterion written down (board renders replay in under N sessions of rework).
> - Update the model ids in the price-table example: `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7` are old; current ids are `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`. Keep the table dated.
>
> ## 4. Section 12, milestones as the mission plan
>
> - The order M0 to M5 is right as the seed of the mission plan, under the delivery model in section 0: one mission, six milestones, one `mission/observatory-v1` branch, one PR at the end.
> - M0 must complete before the orchestrator plans M1 onward in detail: the stream schema is unknown until the capture exists. Plan the rest after M0, from the frozen mapping.
> - M4 (gate and fix loop) needs a repository with a PR flow, CI and rulesets to test against; use a private demo repository with CI rather than the observatory itself, which has no PR flow until the end of the mission.
> - M5's acceptance ("matches a hand-computed reference") needs the reference to exist: a spreadsheet computed by hand from the M0 capture, produced by the human once. Validators cannot invent that oracle.
> - Dogfooding from M1 holds: the mission that builds the observatory is observed in the observatory; its own lane 8 stays empty until the final PR.

**Action:** revise PRD to v0.2 incorporating all points. Card unit changes from feature to milestone; gate becomes the mission's single PR; fix loop reopens the mission on `mission/<name>`, no new PR.

on:

    branches:

  workflow_call:
  workflow_dispatch:

#!/bin/sh
# Reports which tools the Makefile needs and how to install the missing ones.
# Exit 0 always: this is advisory. CI installs its own tools.
set -u

check() {
  name=$1; hint=$2
  if command -v "$name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '  ok       %s\n' "$name"
  else
    printf '  missing  %-18s %s\n' "$name" "$hint"
  fi
}
