input.proposal:
# droid-observatory v1 mission

Builds the Tauri 2 + Leptos desktop app described in `SPEC.md` v0.2 (v0.1 approved by the owner on 2026-10-22; v0.2 adds only the §5.8 concurrency limits the owner ordered). The spec is the authority; this proposal restates it in the mission's terms and records the readiness decisions taken at the planning boundary. Where the proposal and the spec differ, the spec wins and the difference is a bug in this proposal.

## 1. Plan overview

Seven milestones in SPEC §3 order, each integrated into `mission/observatory-v1` (already created from `main` at `c8524c2`, pre-mission commit `2266d3e` holds the readiness reports, SPEC §5.8, AGENTS.md and session-log entries 25–26). One pull request `mission/observatory-v1` → `main` at the end, opened by the orchestrator, merged by the owner when `gate` is green.

| Milestone | Delivers | Cap (USD-eq) |
|---|---|---|
| **S** walking skeleton | workspace `crates/observatory-core`, `crates/observatory-cli`, `apps/observatory-app`; canonical `Event` with `EventKind::Unknown`, `SourcePtr`, `mapping_version`; `observatory-cli replay` printing `unknown events: N`; empty nine-lane Tauri window; `Cargo.lock`, `deny.toml`; `cargo machete` + `cargo llvm-cov` (reported) in `mission-branch.yml`; B-016 version check in `release.yml`; snapshot `fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl`; hybrid backlog (`gh` issues labelled `backlog`, `scripts/gen-backlog.sh`) at integration | 40 |
| **M0** capture and mapping | fixture `2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl` + `.children/` frozen from this mission's own sessions at S integration; `mapping::v1` to PRD §7 kinds; `unknown events: 0` hard gate; SQLite store with pointer index; `inspect <event-id>`; decision files (mapping v1, `--tag`/child-session/role findings, session schema, keyring); coverage gate 80 % enforced from here | 60 |
| **M1** board, replay, attach | nine-lane board, cards by lane, worker sub-lanes, filters, scrubber, unmapped tray, Details Timeline, agent panel; `notify` + poll attach within 1 s; B-006 scrub pass; mission library (FR-L4); **Leptos go/no-go** (≤3 rework sessions, clean Trunk build) | 150 |
| **M2** host | launch screen; spawn `droid exec --mission --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc`; `RpcSource`; pause/message/answer; live output per agent | 80 |
| **M3** intervention | every control a lane-7 event with human actor; stall flag + runbook prompt; `docs/runbooks/stalled-mission.md` revised | 60 |
| **M4** branch, gate, fix loop | `GitSource`, `GitHubSource` behind `Forge`; PR/check/ruleset/attestation detection; merge policy and `policy-merged`; Merge button; fix cycle; demo branch pair `demo/base` + ruleset `demo-gate` + `demo-gate.yml` (label `demo:red`) | 120 |
| **M5** time, waste, cost | time-state engine, rework windows, overhead, waste causes, tokens/cost at `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, budget meter, model comparison, export, Details tabs, lane-9 charts, Grafana OTLP export (≤182 series worst case); oracle test against the owner's `reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv` | 120 |

Total cap 630 USD-eq. At the M0 boundary the orchestrator proposes re-caps for M1–M5 from measured S and M0 usage. M0 is also the gate for detailed M1–M5 planning: M1–M5 features are decomposed coarsely now and refined at the M0 boundary from the frozen mapping, without changing their scope.

## 2. Expected functionality (acceptance per milestone)

Each milestone's named tests (SPEC §3 "Tests green"), acceptance commands and gate are the validation contract's source. Common exit for every milestone: `make check` green on the mission branch after integration, `mission-checks` green on the push, zero blocking findings, SPEC §9/§10 rows, README/BACKLOG/decisions index updated, `reports/usage/<m>.md`, `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json`, `reports/ci/<date>-<m>.md` added, no `unknown.event` on the capture when the milestone adds a source.

Highlights of what the validators must see:
- **S**: `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` ends with `unknown events: N` (N > 0 allowed); `make app-dev` opens nine named empty lanes; `cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file`.
- **M0**: `make replay-fixtures`; replay of the M0 fixture ends with `unknown events: 0`; `inspect` prints the exact raw line by pointer; roles resolve for orchestrator, worker, both validators; children attach to their parent.
- **M1**: board renders the M0 capture in `trunk serve --port 3141` (fixture via file picker) and in the Tauri window; a `droid exec --mission` started in a terminal appears on the board within 1 s; scrubber, filters, tray count = unknown count; mission library lists past captures.
- **M2**: a short hosted mission on a scratch directory inside the worktree; pause/message/answer reach the orchestrator; hosted and attached views agree on event count; child process reaped on window close.
- **M3**: each control emits one lane-7 event; stall flag after `[intervention].stall_threshold_min` of no active time, none under threshold.
- **M4**: `demo/red-1` PR with `demo:red` → check fails → card loops to lane 3 with cycle count 1 → label removed → check green → Merge visible → merge from the app → badge updates → branch deleted; all run ids and PR numbers pasted. Target branch read from config.
- **M5**: `observatory-cli metrics <m0 fixture> --csv` within tolerance (1 s, 1 token, 0.01 USD) of the owner's reference CSV; series appear in the owner's Grafana stack with only the allowed labels; telemetry stays off without the keychain item and the UI says so.

## 3. Architecture (SPEC §5, with planning-boundary refinements)

- **`observatory-core`** (sync, no tokio): `model` (canonical `Event`, `EventKind` incl. `Unknown`, `SourcePtr::Jsonl { path, byte_offset, byte_len }`, `mapping_version` on every event, lanes, roles), `ingest` (`Source` trait; `JsonlSource` for session files reading the JSONL **and its sibling `<id>.settings.json`** for token usage, model, tags and child linkage via `session_start.callingSessionId`; `RpcSource` M2; `GitSource`, `GitHubSource` behind `Forge` M4), `mapping::v1` (selected by the Droid version recorded in the fixture header; `droid --version` 0.247.0 is the target), `store` (rusqlite bundled, pointer index, raw lines never copied), `metrics` (time states, windows, cost, series budget), `view` (card position, filters, scrubber view-models, unit-tested here), `control` (lane-7 semantics), `config` (every threshold from `config/observatory.example.toml`), `secrets` (`keyring-core` 1.0.1 + `apple-native-keyring-store` 1.0.2, generic-password lookup by service `droid-observatory/<name>`, account = login user; OTLP header value parsed as `name=value` on the first `=`; never logged).
- **`observatory-cli`**: `replay`, `inspect`, `metrics --csv` over core; exit codes and the `unknown events: N` line are the oracle the validators compare the UI against.
- **`apps/observatory-app`**: Tauri 2.12 shell (tokio only here: `rt-multi-thread, process, macros`) exposing commands over core; Leptos 0.8 CSR UI built by Trunk 0.22, no logic beyond rendering. Dev URL `http://localhost:3141`.
- **Telemetry**: `opentelemetry` 0.33 + `opentelemetry-otlp` (`http-proto`, `metrics`, `reqwest-blocking-client`) to Grafana Cloud behind `[telemetry].enabled`; label allow-list and the §5.7 budget enforced in core.
- **GitHub access**: fine-grained read-only PAT from the keychain (Contents, Issues, Pull requests, Actions, Commit statuses, Metadata). Check results are read via Actions runs and commit statuses, **not** the check-runs API (no Checks permission). Open point for the M3→M4 boundary: the Merge button needs write on Pull requests; with the current token the app must surface the 403 cleanly, and the owner decides whether to widen the token for the M4 demo.
- **Decision files due at S integration** (owner-approved today): keyring variant B; session schema (no Droid version in files → fixture header; usage in `.settings.json`; sibling child files); read-only PAT → Actions runs + statuses; hybrid backlog; coverage and machete (SPEC §8).

Full detail will be in `architecture.md` in the mission directory.

## 4. Environment setup

Already done and verified on 2026-10-22 (`reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`): Rust 1.99.1 via `rust-toolchain.toml` (rustfmt, clippy, wasm32), trunk 0.22.0, tauri-cli 2.12.4, cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1 + llvm-tools-preview, cargo-machete 0.9.2, cargo-deny 0.20.2, gitleaks, markdownlint-cli2, lychee, actionlint, gh 2.102 (logged in as `dctellya`, admin on the repo), agent-browser 0.37.1, Droid 0.247.0. `make doctor` reports all ok. `make hooks` enabled; `.factory/hooks.json` guards git and logs tool calls.

`init.sh` will only re-run `make doctor` and `make hooks` and verify the worktree exists; nothing is installed per session. Machine quirks workers must know: global `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Users/dct/.cargo/shared_rust_target` with `sccache`, so all cargo builds serialize on one lock; `[profile.dev] opt-level = 1` applies to wasm builds.

## 5. Infrastructure and boundaries

- **Branch/worktree policy (SPEC §2)**: workers and validators of milestone `<m>` work only in `../observatory-wt/<m>` on branch `wt/<m>` (created by the orchestrator from `mission/observatory-v1` when the milestone starts). The orchestrator integrates with `git merge --no-ff wt/<m>`, runs `make check`, pushes, waits for `mission-checks` green, writes the shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md`, `reports/`) and removes the worktree. Two worktrees never edit the same file.
- **Git**: forward only; never amend/reset/rebase/stash/force-push; never push to `main`; never `--no-verify`; commit subject ≤ 72 chars; trailer `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`. Tests first: the red test is committed before the code.
- **Ports**: 3141 for the UI dev server (one `trunk serve` owns it at a time); 3142–3149 for scratch. Off-limits: 5000, 7000, 8000, 11434, 18444–18451 and anything else already listening.
- **Off-limits**: `main` and its `main-gate` ruleset, `rust-toolchain.toml` without a decision file, other worktrees, `~/.cargo/config.toml`, the owner's Ollama/SurrealDB/Docker services, keychain values (read via the API, never printed), `~/.factory/sessions/` is read-only (snapshots are copies into `fixtures/`, committed only after `gitleaks detect --no-git` is clean and a reviewer read them).
- **One outward write**: the demo-pair merge in M4 (from the app, human-confirmed) and the ruleset/branch/label setup for `demo/base` by the orchestrator with `gh`. Nothing else leaves the machine except pushes of `mission/**`, `wt/**`, `demo/**` branches and the final PR.
- **Secrets**: keychain `droid-observatory/github-token` and `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` (both present), `GITHUB_TOKEN` env as fallback for the token only.

## 6. Testing strategy (SPEC §6)

Gate command everywhere: `make check` (markdownlint, lychee, actionlint, file size, debt markers, decisions index, gitleaks, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `make replay-fixtures`, `cargo deny check`, `cargo machete`, `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80` from M0). Suites: unit tests next to code; fixture replay + golden mapping tests in `crates/observatory-core/tests/`; attach latency harness; CLI tests; metrics oracle (M5); telemetry budget (M5). UI logic is unit-tested in core; no wasm test runner. Scrutiny validators check that each feature's red test run exists in the worker log (rule 1). CI: `mission-branch.yml` aggregate `mission-checks` (budget 3 min warm, wall time pasted to `reports/ci/`), `demo-gate.yml` (M4), `gate.yml` on the final PR.

## 7. User testing strategy

Verified executable on 2026-10-22 (`reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`):
- **Browser surface (primary)**: `trunk serve --config <ui Trunk.toml> --port 3141 --open false` (55.9 s cold, 1.5–2.1 s incremental); validators drive it with `agent-browser` (open, snapshot, click, screenshot, console/errors), isolated per `--session`. Fixtures are opened through the file picker. Evidence: screenshots, snapshot refs, console errors, CLI output as oracle.
- **Tauri surface (smoke check)**: `make app-dev` (37.7 s to running app). agent-browser cannot attach to WKWebView; evidence is process alive, `Running` log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing, plus `screencapture` when the display is unlocked. At each milestone integration the owner takes one real screenshot with the display unlocked and it is attached to the report (owner decision).
- **Live attach/host**: a `droid exec --mission` on a scratch directory inside the worktree, with timestamps from the attach-latency test and validator clocks.
- **Concurrency (SPEC §5.8 v0.2)**: at most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (~1.5 GB RSS each); `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores); cargo builds serialize on the shared target lock; `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when one trunk owns 3141. Validators run user tests only after builds finish.

## 8. Mission readiness

- Toolchain and crates verified (§4 above); Tauri 2 + Leptos CSR scaffold builds and runs; DMG bundling only in the CI `bundle` job (fails non-interactively locally).
- Grafana OTLP endpoint answers 200 with the parsed keychain header.
- GitHub rulesets and Actions APIs answer under the owner's `gh` auth; `main-gate` ruleset present; the token can create `demo-gate`.
- Session file schema inspected (14 JSONL files in the mission's sessions dir at check time); the capture plan (B-010) is feasible from this mission's own sessions.
- Validation path executable end to end: `make check` exit 0 on the mission branch; agent-browser drove the scaffold on 3141 with zero console errors.
- Human inputs still scheduled (SPEC §2): M1 go/no-go, M0-boundary re-caps, M3→M4 token write permission question, M4→M5 reference CSV, final PR merge. Model ids per `.factory/settings.json` (orchestrator `claude-fable-5.1`, workers `claude-sonnet-5-5`, validators `claude-opus-5-5`, all `high`).

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- Attach-to-render latency < 1 s per event; `mission-checks` warm < 3 min; `observatory-core` line coverage ≥ 80 % from M0; telemetry series ≤ 182 worst case (< 200); no `unknown.event` dropped, count always visible; raw lines read-only, never uploaded or copied into the store; secrets only from keychain/env, never in repo, store or logs; every threshold in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason; every count/timing pasted from a tool; files > 200 KB only under `fixtures/streams/` and `build-log/`; `cargo deny` clean on every dependency; budget caps per milestone with the stall flag at a cap.

content.thinking:
The mission got approved with four comments to resolve. For the budget-versus-plan point, I need to specify that hitting a throttle pauses at the boundary rather than silently downgrading the model, while keeping the M0 re-cap step intact — I'll write this into mission.md and AGENTS.md now.

For M4 acceptance, the merge button should only appear when policy allows it, with a clean 403 shown for read-only tokens, merges happening by owner via UI or API, and the badge refreshing from polling — this contradicts SPEC §3's "merge from the app" language, so I'll treat the owner's decision as superseding and log it as a SPEC as-built amendment at integration time.

For reasoning effort, there's a conflict between §8 saying all-high and the owner now saying workers should be medium, so I need to check `.factory/settings.json` to see what workerReasoningEffort is actually set to and reconcile it against the SPEC §2 table's "high" decision from October 22nd.

If settings.json shows medium while SPEC says high, I'll fix the config to match SPEC and log the change as a repo fix on the mission branch, then move to the backlog question — the owner wants to drop the hybrid GitHub-issues approach and use BACKLOG.md exclusively, which means reverting the hybrid backlog language introduced in PR #23 back to a BACKLOG.md-only model, affecting SPEC §8 and RULES rule 14.

Since RULES.md is technically the owner's file, I'll flag that rule 14 still reads "hybrid" and needs the owner's wording update or their approval for me to make the edit directly, while recording BACKLOG.md-only as the agreed direction in the shared-file update at S integration.

I also need to update the AGENTS.md backlog line in the repo as an orchestrator-owned change on the mission branch, which I'll bundle with the settings.json check into a later worker task alongside pre-mission commit 2 and Entry 27 — confirming workers operate out of worktrees rather than the repo root. Turning to the actual artifact authoring now, I'm mapping out the sequence: verify settings.json's reasoning effort, update the auto-created mission.md with the four corrections, then tackle architecture.md, weighing whether to write it myself or delegate to the architect role.

Since architecture.md is large and the guidance allows delegating drafting as long as full context is provided, I'll have a worker draft it using SPEC §5 and the readiness findings as a base, then review it myself to conserve context. For validation-contract.md, I'll split the work across per-area subagents writing into contract-work/, synthesize their output, then review; validation-state.json can be generated by a subagent directly. For features.json, I need to author it myself since every assertion must be claimed — given this mission's seven milestones, the contract could have 100+ assertions, so I'll map features to SPEC §3 and have a subagent run a coverage check afterward.

Now I'm turning to AGENTS.md, mission skills, services.yaml, init.sh, and the library directory, defining worker types like a core-worker for Rust/CLI work and a ui-worker for the Leptos/Tauri app. I'm wrestling with how integration work fits — the SPEC implies the orchestrator itself handles merges and shared files, but since the orchestrator shouldn't do hands-on work directly, I'm considering whether a Task subagent acting under my direction (rather than a formal mission worker) satisfies that requirement, versus defining a dedicated integration-worker skill for the merge/report job.

I'm also figuring out the timing: milestone validators need to run in the worktree before integration happens, and start_mission_run only returns at specific checkpoints like handoffs or full completion, so there's no natural hook between milestones. My plan is to make the first feature of each subsequent milestone a "milestone-setup" feature using an integration-worker skill that merges the previous milestone's worktree into the mission branch, runs checks, pushes, waits on CI, writes shared files and reports, and cleans up the old worktree.

Then I'm tracing the feature ordering: since validators get injected after a milestone's features finish, a feature named "integrate" placed as the first feature of the next milestone will run exactly after those validators pass, giving the sequence I need across S, M0 through M5. The one wrinkle is the very last milestone, M5 — its integration and PR step would need its own trailing milestone to get validators injected, which works but adds overhead, so I'm weighing whether that's acceptable or if there's a cleaner way to handle the final step.

The M0 fixture freeze probably belongs as the first implementation feature right after integration, snapshotting the sessions directory into fixtures within the worktree, since timing lines up either way.

Now I'm sketching out the worker types: a core-worker for Rust/CLI features with TDD and worktree discipline, and a ui-worker for the Leptos side.

For the ui-worker specifically, it handles the Leptos UI and Tauri shell, running trunk serve plus agent-browser self-checks and TDD against the view-model in core. I'm also weighing an infra-worker for CI, Makefile, deny checks, scripts, and demo branch setup, and an integration-worker for milestone boundaries like merging, pushing, and worktree lifecycle — deciding four distinct skills are justified since each has its own procedures, even if it means a bit more maintenance. I also need to note that the scrutiny and user-testing validators will require a library/user-testing.md file.

Since validators must run inside the milestone's worktree, I'm thinking about how services.yaml should handle paths that vary per milestone rather than being static with a hardcoded port — considering a stable symlink like observatory-wt/current that the integration worker updates to point at the active worktree, so services.yaml can reference a fixed path instead of needing environment variables.

I'm weighing whether the worktree-per-milestone policy is overkill given features run sequentially with only one active worktree at a time, but deciding to keep it per spec with the symlink approach, verified by init.sh.

On the throttle issue, I need to note that when the runner hits a usage limit, it pauses and waits for the owner rather than switching models, recording the usage state and setting a stall flag in mission.md.

For planning ahead, I'll draft M1–M5 features now at a reasonable level of detail since SPEC §3 already covers it well, refining further once the M0 boundary is reached. First step is checking settings.json and mission.md, listing the mission directory, then launching parallel subagents to draft architecture.md and area-specific contracts — core/CLI, board/attach UI, host/intervention, git/github/demo, metrics/telemetry, plus cross-area process gates — each writing assertions to contract-work files before a synthesizer merges them.

I need to equip each subagent with substantial context: the SPEC path for them to read directly, readiness report paths, owner decisions, tool choices, and ID prefix conventions. Let me run the quick checks first.

I'll work through the four review comments: documenting throttle behavior, correcting the M4 exit criteria, verifying reasoning effort settings against SPEC §2, and switching the backlog approach to BACKLOG.md only (proposing wording for RULES.md rule 14 since that's your file).

**Design choices made beyond what the sources fix (10 lines):**

1. Fixture header is a sidecar `<date>-<slug>.capture.json` (fields: `droid_version`, `captured_at`, `source_dir`, `sessions[{id, role, file}]`, `mapping_version`), not a first line, so the `.jsonl` stays byte-identical and golden `byte_offset`s match the live file.
2. `Source` trait is `next_batch() -> Result<Vec<RawRecord>>` plus `at_eof()`, replacing SPEC's `poll`; the CLI stops at EOF and the watcher keeps calling, which makes replay and attach literally one code path (D-008).
3. Core Cargo features (`store`, `watch`, `rpc`, `github`, `secrets`) with the UI depending on core `default-features = false`, so `model`/`mapping`/`view`/`metrics` compile to wasm and the browser host (`trunk serve` 3141, SPEC §6) can open a fixture through the file picker with a `BrowserBackend`; `TauriBackend` uses the same UI code.
4. `EventId` is deterministic `<session_id>:<byte_offset>:<sub>` (no hash crate); `MissionId` = root session id until M0 confirms where `--tag` lives; added `Role::Unresolved` so a child session whose role cannot be resolved stays visible and counted instead of being guessed.
5. `EventKind` serde is the derived externally-tagged `snake_case` form (`"finding_blocking"`, `{"unknown":{"raw_type":…}}`) with `prd_name()` for the dotted display/store name; `Event` uses `deny_unknown_fields` so golden drift fails loudly.
6. Hosted (M2) stdout lines are spooled verbatim to `~/.droid-observatory/hosted/<launch-id>.jsonl`, and `SourcePtr::Rpc { path, byte_offset, byte_len }` points into it, so `inspect`/Details have a raw line for RPC events without copying any Droid file.
7. HTTP client for GitHub is blocking `ureq` (core has no tokio); new config keys `[github].target_branch = "main"` and `[github].repo = "dctellya/droid-observatory"` so the target is parameterised as the M4 test demands; `[ingest].startup_scan_hours = 24` bounds the startup scan.
8. Lane-7 control events reuse only the five PRD kinds (`ApprovalGiven`, `QuestionAnswered`, `PrMergedByHuman`); the control name lives in `human_actions.kind`, free text is never stored (only its length).
9. The OTel exporter lives in `src-tauri/telemetry.rs` (tokio-flavoured SDK) while `core::telemetry` is pure (series plan, 182 worst case, label allow-list, `name=value` header split on the first `=`); Active time intervals come from mapper-set `duration` (tool_use→tool_result, previous line→assistant message), to be validated by the M5 oracle.
10. The oracle CSV column contract is fixed now (`scope,id,name,cycle_s,first_pass_active_s,rework_s,waste_*_s ×8,rework_windows,tokens_*,cost_usd,price_table`) so the owner can produce `reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv` before M5; coverage runs as a separate `coverage` CI job with `COVERAGE_MIN` (0 in S, 80 from M0) and a `make coverage` target kept out of `make check` because `cargo llvm-cov` must run alone.

content.thinking:
That totals around 287 assertions across the milestones, which is a lot given the guidance, so there's real risk of over-assertion and heavier validation cost. I'll have the synthesizer merge everything and dedupe repeated checks like red-before-green, make check, and coverage that show up across multiple milestones and in PROC.

I'm now wrestling with whether per-milestone process assertions belong in PROC alone or duplicated in each area — the area-specific ones seem to just restate PROC's checks, so I should strip them from the areas and keep PROC as the mission-wide source of truth. But the harder problem is who validates a PROC assertion that spans milestones, since each assertion needs exactly one feature owner and a mission-wide merge check can't naturally map to a single milestone's integration step.

My solution is to add a `final` milestone with a single `final-integrate-m5-and-open-pr` feature that claims the cross-cutting PROC assertions (and PR-opened checks), so it picks up the usual validator chain instead of going unchecked — the human still does the actual merge afterward. This adds one extra validation round but gives the process gates real coverage; I still need to sort out the per-milestone-instance assertions like the per-milestone usage reports.

For deduplication, I'm having the synthesizer strip out area-level process assertions that just restate PROC rules (red-before-green, exit codes, coverage thresholds, worktree identity, commit hygiene), keeping only the gates that are truly area-specific, like unknown events, oracle checks, and go/no-go decisions. I also want to make sure coverage gets asserted exactly once per milestone starting from m0, and I need to check for any unsupported additions the architecture doesn't actually call for.

I'm deciding some borderline additions are acceptable as minimal, low-cost observability — request logging around GitHub calls (method, URL, status, no headers) and tracing lines for session discovery and event appending — so I'll fold these into the architecture sections rather than treating them as scope creep. With that settled, the total assertion count should land around 240, which feels reasonable for a seven-milestone mission, and now the synthesizer's job is to merge everything into validation-contract.md with a clear header and area ordering.

After dedupe I need IDs renumbered sequentially since nothing references them yet, plus outputs of validation-state.json and a per-area summary index for feature authoring. I also want the synthesizer running review checks for contradictions, duplicates, over-broad "all/every" claims, testability, and scope, reporting anything removed, merged, or flagged rather than silently adding new assertions. In parallel I'm weighing whether I should personally author the skills, services.yaml, init.sh, library, and AGENTS.md — that's a heavy writing load given my context budget.

Since skills are the core worker procedures I'm meant to design, I'll write those myself concisely, but delegate AGENTS.md, library, services, and init to a worker given planning-notes and architecture context. Rather than blocking by awaiting tasks sequentially, I'm considering launching both the synthesizer and artifact-worker tasks in the background and writing the skills myself while they run, then checking results afterward.

All seven area drafts are complete (287 assertions before dedup, checked against the PROC section). Now I'll kick off synthesis/review and runtime-artifact drafting in the background while I write the worker skills.

You implement one infrastructure feature for the droid-observatory mission inside the milestone worktree:
workspace and crate scaffolding, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `deny.toml`, scripts, fixture
capture, or GitHub test infrastructure (M4 demo branch pair). Infrastructure is tested too: a workflow
change is tested with `actionlint` and a dry run of the job's commands locally; a Makefile target by
running it; a fixture by `make replay-fixtures` and `gitleaks detect --no-git`.

## Common procedure for every implementation worker (read fully)

### 0. Where you work
- Your feature names a `milestone` (`s`, `m0`, `m1`, `m2`, `m3`, `m4`, `m5`). You work ONLY in the
  worktree `/Users/dct/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current` (a symlink to
  `../observatory-wt/<milestone>` on branch `wt/<milestone>`). Run

  and confirm it prints `wt/<your milestone>`. If it does not, or the symlink is missing, STOP and
  hand off with `returnToOrchestrator: true` and the observed state. Never create worktrees yourself.
- `cd` into the worktree for every command. Never edit the main checkout
  (`/Users/dct/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`, branch `mission/observatory-v1`).
- Never touch: `main`, `SPEC.md`, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `reports/`, `rust-toolchain.toml`,

  copies only via the fixture procedure). Deferred work goes to the handoff `discoveredIssues` with a
  reason; the orchestrator moves it to `BACKLOG.md` at integration (never GitHub issues).
- Read before coding: `{missionDir}/architecture.md` (authoritative design), the assertions your feature
  `fulfills` in `{missionDir}/validation-contract.md`, `{missionDir}/library/rust-conventions.md`,
  `{missionDir}/library/environment.md`, and `SPEC.md` §3 for your milestone (named tests, acceptance
  commands, "must not touch").

### 1. Tests first (RULES rule 1, enforced by scrutiny)
For each behaviour in the feature:
1. Write the test (name reads as a sentence; use the SPEC-named test when one exists). Run it and
   confirm it FAILS for the right reason. The failing run must appear in your tool log (the hook
   writes `build-log/`), so run it with the real command (`cargo test -p <crate> <name>`).
2. Commit the red test alone: subject `test(<crate>): red: <test_name>` (≤ 72 chars), body optional,
   trailer `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.
   A red test that does not compile is acceptable only if the commit message says `(does not compile)`.
3. Implement the minimum that turns it green. Commit: `feat(<crate>): <what>` (or `fix(...)`,
   `ci(...)`, `docs(...)`), same trailer.
Never squash red and green into one commit; never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push; never
`--no-verify`. Fix mistakes with a new commit.

### 2. Dependencies (rule 3)
Only versions from `architecture.md` §13 (verified 2026-10-22). Any other crate: verify the version on
crates.io the same day, run `make deny` before committing, and note it in the handoff. Core (`observatory-core`)
never depends on tokio. If `make deny` fails on a dependency, do not add it; hand off with the finding.

### 3. Config and numbers (rules 7, 18)
Every threshold or limit comes from `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason comment, loaded through
`core::config`. Never estimate a count, timing, or size in code comments, docs, or the handoff: paste the tool's
output. Unknown events are counted and shown, never dropped.

### 4. Before handing off
1. `cd <worktree> && make check` must exit 0. Paste the exit code and the test summary line
   (`test result: ok. N passed; 0 failed`) into the handoff. If a `make check` target is broken for
   reasons outside your feature, stop and hand off with the output; do not patch the Makefile unless
   your feature owns it.
2. If your feature touched `observatory-core` and the milestone is `m0` or later, run
   `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80` ALONE (no other cargo process running) and
   paste the `TOTAL` line.
3. Run the acceptance commands your `fulfills` assertions name and paste their output (e.g. the final
   `unknown events: N` line). For UI features see the ui-worker self-check.
4. `git -C <worktree> status --short` must be clean; `git log --oneline <base>..HEAD` must show the
   red/green pairs. Include the last commit id as `commitId` and the worktree path as `repoPath`.
5. Decision files: if your feature's description tells you to write `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md`
   (format: `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`, Context, Decision, Alternatives, Consequences), pick the next free
   number by listing `docs/decisions/`, write it, run `make decisions-index`, and commit both files
   (`docs(decisions): D-NNN <slug>`). Milestones are sequential, so no other worktree edits the index.

### 5. Handoff fields (in addition to the base handoff)
- `worktree`: path and branch.
- `redGreenPairs`: list of `{ test, redCommit, greenCommit }`.
- `makeCheck`: exit code and the `test result:` summary line(s).

  phrase them as backlog entries (`B-NNN` is assigned by the orchestrator).

## infra-worker specifics

### Reading order
1. `architecture.md` §2 (workspace layout), §4 (fixture layout and `.capture.json` header), §13

# integration-worker

You run the boundary between two milestones. You are the only worker that works in the main checkout
`/Users/dct/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory` on branch `mission/observatory-v1` and the
only one allowed to edit the shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
`docs/decisions/README.md`, `reports/`, `ai/session/`). You never write application code. Your feature
names `previous` (the milestone to integrate, e.g. `s`) and `next` (the worktree to create, e.g. `m0`).
Read `{missionDir}/library/integration-and-boundaries.md` first; it has the commands in detail.

## Preconditions (verify, do not assume)
1. `{missionDir}/validation-state.json`: every assertion claimed by features of milestone `previous` is
   `passed`. If not, STOP and hand off `returnToOrchestrator: true` with the list.
2. `git -C <repo> branch --show-current` is `mission/observatory-v1`; `git status --short` is clean
   except files you are about to write.
3. `git -C ../observatory-wt/<previous> status --short` is clean; note its head commit.

## Procedure
1. **Merge**: `git merge --no-ff wt/<previous> -m "Integrate <previous>: <one-line summary>"` with the
   co-author trailer. Resolve nothing by hand: a conflict means a shared-file violation; hand off with the
   conflicting paths.
2. **Local gate**: `make check` exit 0 on the mission branch (paste). If `make check` fails on the merged
   tree, do not fix code: hand off with the output (the orchestrator schedules a fix feature in the next
   milestone's worktree).
3. **Push and CI**: `git push origin mission/observatory-v1` and `git push origin wt/<previous>` (history).
   Then `gh run list --branch mission/observatory-v1 --limit 3` and `gh run watch <id> --exit-status` for the
   `mission-checks` run. Paste run id, conclusion, and wall time (`createdAt` → `updatedAt`). Red CI: hand off
   with the failing job log excerpt; do not retry blindly.
4. **Reports** (pasted numbers only; `reports/README.md` conventions):
   - `reports/usage/<previous>.md`: tokens, Factory credits and USD-eq per role and model for the sessions of
     this milestone, from the mission sessions' `.settings.json` (`tokenUsage`, `childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId`)
     in `~/.factory/sessions/-Users-dct-code-EllyaOrg-projects-dalimaray-droid-observatory/`, priced with
     `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`; compare with the cap (S 40, M0 60, M1 150, M2 80, M3 60, M4 120, M5 120).
     State the session ids used. Where a number is not visible, write "not exposed", never a guess.
   - `reports/readiness/<date>-<previous>.json` per the existing readiness JSON shape.
   - `reports/ci/<date>-<previous>.md`: run id, wall time of `mission-checks`, per-job durations
     (`gh run view <id> --json jobs`), 3 min warm budget verdict.
   - `reports/screenshots/`: record the expected path `<date>-<previous>.png` for the owner's unlocked-display
     screenshot in the session log entry; the owner adds the file at the boundary.
5. **Shared files**: SPEC §9 (one row: what the human said at the last boundary) and §10 (as-built notes:
   decisions this milestone, deviations, amendments such as planning-note items 1, 7, 9 at S); `README.md`
   (clean-clone commands if they changed, demo branch pair at M4, honest time and usage per milestone from
   `reports/usage/`); `BACKLOG.md` (new `B-NNN` entries from handoffs' `discoveredIssues`/`whatWasLeftUndone`
   with reasons; items settled marked done with the reason); `make decisions-index` if a decision file arrived
   without an index update. Markdown must pass `make check-docs check-links`.
6. **Session log**: append the next `## Entry NN — <previous> integrated` to `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md`
   in the style of entries 24–26: what was integrated, commit ids, run id and wall time, usage vs cap, open
   boundary questions for the human, the screenshot path.
7. **Commit** on the mission branch (`chore(integration): <previous> boundary reports and shared files`, trailer),
   `make check` once more, push.
8. **Worktree rotation**: `git worktree remove ../observatory-wt/<previous>` (branch stays);
   `git worktree add ../observatory-wt/<next> -b wt/<next> mission/observatory-v1`;
   `ln -sfn ../observatory-wt/<next> ../observatory-wt/current` (verify
   `readlink ../observatory-wt/current` and `git -C ../observatory-wt/current branch --show-current`
   prints `wt/<next>`). For `next = final` (after M5), skip the worktree and instead open the PR:
   `gh pr create --base main --head mission/observatory-v1 --title "..." --body-file <file>`, paste the PR number
   and wait for `gate` with `gh pr checks <n> --watch`; do not merge.
9. **Boundary report**: hand off with `returnToOrchestrator: true` and `boundaryReport`: usage vs cap, CI
   result, decisions written, deviations proposed (with reason and cost), questions for the human for this
   boundary (M0: proposed re-caps for M1–M5 from measured S and M0 usage; M1: go/no-go evidence; M3→M4:
   write-token question; M4→M5: reference CSV presence), and the screenshot path to request.

## Never
- Amend, reset, rebase, stash, force-push, push to `main`, merge the final PR, disable a hook, estimate a
  number, create GitHub issues, or change a model/effort setting.

// @input: agents <<'AG'
# AGENTS.md — droid-observatory v1 mission

Operational guidance for every worker and validator. Precedence: `ai/RULES.md` (repo) > this file's
boundaries > `planning-notes.md` (owner decisions after the spec) > `SPEC.md` v0.2 > PRD v0.6. The design
is `architecture.md`; the definition of done is `validation-contract.md`. Commands and services live in
`services.yaml`. Mission objectives are in `mission.md`, not here.

## Mission Boundaries (NEVER VIOLATE)

**Repository and branches**
- Repo: `/Users/dct/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`, mission branch `mission/observatory-v1`.
- Implementation workers and validators work ONLY in the active worktree
  `/Users/dct/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current` → `../observatory-wt/<m>` on `wt/<m>`.
  Only the `integration-worker` (and the orchestrator) touches the main checkout and the shared files
  `SPEC.md`, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md` (workers may regenerate it with
  `make decisions-index` after adding a decision file, because milestones are sequential), `reports/`, `ai/session/`.
- Never write to `main`, never touch ruleset `main-gate` (id 25636994), never open or merge a PR to `main`
  (the orchestrator opens the single final PR; the owner merges it).
- Git is forward-only: no amend, reset, rebase, stash, force-push, `--no-verify`, or hook changes. Hooks
  `.githooks/*` and `.factory/hooks.json` stay enabled. Commit subject ≤ 72 chars, trailer
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.
- `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1) and `.factory/settings.json` (models/effort) change only by decision file
  approved by the owner. No silent model or reasoning-effort change, ever.

**Ports**: 3141 for the UI dev server (exactly one `trunk serve` owns it); 3142–3149 scratch. Off-limits:
5000, 7000, 8000 (SurrealDB), 11434 (Ollama), 18444–18451, and anything already listening
(check `lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN` before binding).

**Off-limits resources**: `~/.cargo/config.toml`; `~/.factory/sessions/` (read-only; fixtures are `cp` copies
committed only after `gitleaks detect --no-git` is clean and the files were read by a reviewer); the owner's
Docker, Ollama and SurrealDB services; keychain values (read through `core::secrets` or
`security find-generic-password -s <service>` WITHOUT `-w`; never print, log, or copy them); the live Grafana
stack beyond the M5 export test; GitHub Issues (none are created: backlog is `BACKLOG.md` only).

**Outward writes allowed**: pushes of `mission/**`, `wt/**`, `demo/**` branches; M4 demo infrastructure via
`gh` (`demo/base`, label `demo:red`, ruleset `demo-gate`, PRs `demo/*` → `demo/base`); the final PR by the
orchestrator. Nothing else leaves the machine.

Workers: if your feature cannot be completed inside these boundaries, hand off with
`returnToOrchestrator: true` and say why. Never violate a boundary to finish.

## Mission Directives

**Tools**: `make check` is the only local gate (same as CI `mission-checks`). `cargo llvm-cov -p
observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80` from M0 (run alone). `agent-browser` 0.37.1 for the browser host on
3141. `gh` 2.102 (owner's auth) for GitHub reads and the demo pair. `sqlite3` for the store. `actionlint`,
`gitleaks`, `markdownlint-cli2`, `lychee` through the Makefile.

**Skills**: `core-worker`, `ui-worker`, `infra-worker`, `integration-worker` as assigned per feature; each
worker invokes its skill after `mission-worker-base`. Validators follow `library/user-testing.md`.

**Dependencies** (versions verified 2026-10-22, table in `architecture.md` §13): Rust 1.99.1; tauri 2.12.5,
tauri-cli 2.12.4, leptos 0.8.22 (csr), trunk 0.22.0, notify 8.2.0, serde 1.0.229, serde_json 1.0.154,
rusqlite 0.40.2 (bundled), tokio 1.54.1 (app/host only), keyring-core 1.0.1 + apple-native-keyring-store 1.0.2
(never `keyring` 4.x), opentelemetry* 0.33.1, tracing-opentelemetry 0.34.0, tracing 0.1.44,
tracing-subscriber 0.3.23, cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1, cargo-machete 0.9.2, cargo-deny 0.20.2. Any other crate:
version verified on the day, `make deny` green, noted in the handoff.

**Owner decisions after the spec** (binding; full text in `planning-notes.md`):
1. Mapping version is selected from the Droid version in the fixture `.capture.json` header; usage, model,
   tags and child links come from the sibling `<id>.settings.json`.
2. Keyring variant B (above). 3. DMG only in CI. 4. Tauri window is a smoke check; the browser host is the
   primary interactive surface; the owner adds one unlocked-display screenshot per integration.
5. Concurrency limits (below). 6. GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT: read checks through Actions
   runs and commit statuses, never the check-runs API. 7. M4 exit: Merge button visible when policy allows;
   the app surfaces the 403 cleanly; the owner merges; the badge updates from the poll.
8. At a usage throttle or a milestone cap the run pauses, usage so far is written to `reports/usage/`, the
   stall flag goes up and the owner is asked; no model/effort downgrade. 9. Backlog is `BACKLOG.md` only.

**Other rules**
- Tests first (rule 1): red test committed before the green code, every feature. Scrutiny checks the
  `test result: FAILED` run in `build-log/` and the commit order.
- Numbers are pasted from tools, never estimated (rule 7). Unknown events are counted and shown (rule 18).
- Every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason. `TODO(B-NNN)` only.
- `observatory-core` has no tokio; the UI has no logic; raw session lines are never stored or uploaded.
- Deferred work goes into the handoff as a backlog-shaped entry with a reason; the integration writes it to
  `BACKLOG.md`.
- Files > 200 KB only under `fixtures/streams/` and `build-log/` (`scripts/check-file-size.sh` is the source).

## Runtime limits (measured 2026-10-22, SPEC §5.8)

- Max 3 concurrent `agent-browser` sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34–1.54 GB RSS each).
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the readiness run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock; do not start a second cargo build and
  expect progress. `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns 3141.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46–2.08 s; `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- Killing `cargo-tauri` orphans `trunk serve` and the app binary: kill all three PIDs.

## Testing & Validation Guidance

Validators treat this section as authoritative; details and exact commands are in `library/user-testing.md`.

- Work in the active worktree (`observatory-wt/current`); never in the main checkout.
- Browser host first: `services.yaml` `trunk-ui` on 3141, drive with `agent-browser --session <name>`;
